decisions.title: LLM never touches HTML
decisions.decision: All LLM input and output is JSON only. pipeline-render.js converts JSON to HTML deterministically.
decisions.rationale: Prevents broken markup. Enables model swapping without touching HTML. Guarantees structural consistency across all pages.

decisions.title: Model config in config/models.json
decisions.decision: All LLM model assignments live in config/models.json. Scripts read at startup.
decisions.rationale: Change models without touching code. Enables environment-based overrides (prod/test/dev).

decisions.title: OpenRouter as API provider
decisions.decision: Route all LLM calls through OpenRouter rather than direct provider APIs.
decisions.alternatives: Direct Anthropic API, direct OpenAI API
decisions.rationale: Model flexibility — can compare Haiku vs Sonnet vs Grok without changing auth. Cost comparison across providers. Single API key.

decisions.title: pipeline-* prefix for production scripts
decisions.decision: All scripts that run regularly in production use pipeline-* naming. Utility scripts have no prefix or live in scripts/utils/.
decisions.rationale: Clear distinction between production workflow and maintenance utilities at a glance.

decisions.title: data/reviews/ as canonical JSON source
decisions.decision: After pipeline runs, data/reviews/ is the source of truth. pipeline/ folders are scratch space — safe to delete and regenerate.
decisions.rationale: Clean separation between working space and final output. Enables safe pipeline reruns.

decisions.title: config/nav.json as single source of truth for navigation
decisions.decision: All pipeline scripts read nav from config/nav.json. check-nav.js audits consistency.
decisions.rationale: One change updates all pages. check-nav.js catches drift immediately.

decisions.title: Netlify for hosting (current)
decisions.decision: Deploy static HTML to Netlify. 301 redirects via netlify.toml for .html URLs.
decisions.rationale: Free tier sufficient at current scale. Simple static deploy. Planned migration to Vercel when database is needed.

decisions.title: Vercel migration planned post-revenue
decisions.decision: Migrate to Vercel once site reaches consistent revenue. Not before.
decisions.rationale: Vercel enables cron jobs (pipeline-guide.js nightly), serverless functions (GSC API), and Postgres database. Not needed until scale justifies complexity.

decisions.title: Dashboard as self-contained microservice in dashboard/
decisions.decision: dashboard/index.html + dashboard/latest.json as standalone folder. Fetches latest.json relative to itself.
decisions.alternatives: Integrate into main pipeline, use data/dashboard/
decisions.rationale: Easy to move or wire up to GSC API on Vercel. No dependencies on pipeline. Friends can view at /dashboard without understanding the project.

decisions.title: Two-stage greenfield generation
decisions.decision: Greenfield pipeline uses two stages — Stage 1 factual (Haiku), Stage 2 editorial (Haiku/Sonnet).
decisions.rationale: Stage 1 verifies factual accuracy before spending tokens on editorial content. Allows human review between stages.

decisions.title: Minimal greenfield input — 5 fields only
decisions.decision: Greenfield input JSON requires only: bookTitle, slug, affiliateLink, youtubeId, videoAffiliateLink.
decisions.alternatives: Full brief with author, director, genre etc.
decisions.rationale: LLM researches and generates everything else. Minimises manual data entry. Helper can populate inputs without understanding the pipeline.

decisions.title: Pillar pages separate from review pages
decisions.decision: Pillar pages have their own pipeline (pipeline-pillar.js), config (config/pillars.json), and data store (data/pillars/).
decisions.alternatives: Reuse review pipeline with a different template
decisions.rationale: Different content type, different generation approach, different rendering requirements. Clean separation avoids contaminating review pipeline.

decisions.title: Hub-and-pillar architecture
decisions.decision: Build topic-level pillar pages above individual review pages. Start with 10 pillars covering broad informational queries.
decisions.alternatives: Review pages only, genre hub pages only
decisions.rationale: GSC data shows query clusters (Lonesome Dove universe, thriller comparisons) with no authority page to consolidate them. Pillar pages capture topic-level traffic and funnel to reviews.

decisions.title: Featured hub at /featured not SEO hub
decisions.decision: /featured is a curated editorial page listing spotlight pages. Not an SEO hub in the hub-and-pillar sense.
decisions.alternatives: Make /featured an SEO hub targeting "best book vs movie" queries
decisions.rationale: Featured serves navigation and editorial positioning. SEO hubs (/book-vs-movie, /thriller) are a separate workstream post-Vercel migration.

decisions.title: Beehiiv over Mailchimp/ConvertKit
decisions.decision: Use Beehiiv for newsletter. Embed form via iframe in pipeline-render.js footer.
decisions.alternatives: Mailchimp (paid after 500 subscribers), ConvertKit/Kit (pricing confusion), custom form
decisions.rationale: Beehiiv free plan sufficient for current stage. Clean embed code. Newsletter brand (Verdict Drop Fridays) already configured.

decisions.title: Newsletter embed in pipeline-render.js footer
decisions.decision: Beehiiv iframe rendered via renderFooter() in pipeline-render.js — appears on all review pages above the footer.
decisions.alternatives: Manual embed on specific pages only, sidebar placement
decisions.rationale: Maximum subscriber capture. Consistent placement. One code change updates all 171 pages on next render.

decisions.title: RavensEdge AI LLC as operating entity
decisions.decision: All site accounts (Amazon Associates, GSC, Netlify, Beehiiv, domain) to be transferred to RavensEdge AI LLC.
decisions.rationale: Business liability separation. Professional affiliate account management.

decisions.title: Amazon Associates tracking ID: readingtheill-20
decisions.decision: Single tracking ID for all Amazon affiliate links across the site.
decisions.rationale: Simplicity. All revenue attributed to one account. ID is public — embedded in all page HTML.
